title: Cohort-based SLI Runway Planner & Initiative Phases
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: We manage SLOs and error budgets globally today which obscures localized reliability regressions (by customer tier, region, or workload). This makes prioritization of reliability initiatives noisy and slows down targeted remediation. Goal: introduce a cohort-based SLI runway planner that lets PMs and SREs create initiatives that track error-budget runway per cohort, automatically break initiatives into time-boxed tranches, and surface gating recommendations (hold/release) based on remaining runway and regression signals. The planner should integrate with Redwood Console SLI dashboards, the incident playbook, and the initiative board so owners can run focused actions with clear acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort creation UI in Console where PMs/SREs can define cohorts by labels: customer_tier, region, model_family, route
Dashboard view that displays error-budget runway (days remaining) for each cohort and highlights cohorts with runway < 7 days
Initiative creation flow that attaches one or more cohorts and suggests tranche length based on historical SLI burn-rate
Automated gating rules: recommend pause of new feature rollouts when cohort runway < 3 days; recommendation must be visible and linkable from the rollout page
Integration tests with runtime telemetry such that cohort SLIs refresh within 1 minute of metric ingestion and rollup accuracy is within 2% of raw data
Playbook link added to initiatives that auto-populates postmortem checklist and owners when an SLO breach occurs
End-to-end E2E doc and a demo recorded for the March reliability review
tasks: Design cohort selector UX and example templates (regional, tiered, model-family)
Backend: cohort service + query layer for fast SLI aggregation (ENG-5023)
Console: cohort dashboard and initiative creation screens (ENG-5310)
Policy engine: implement gating rule evaluator and rollout recommendation hooks
Automation: create webhook pipeline to notify PagerDuty channels and Slack ops when runway thresholds cross
Analytics: add cohort SLI to the monthly reliability report and OKR dashboard
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-01-28: Use cohort definitions as label queries rather than hard lists to keep runtime evaluation flexible
Trade-off: Pre-aggregating cohort SLIs reduces query latency but increases storage cost; start with nearline aggregation every minute and iterate based on perf data
Feedback from SRE (Dana Rodriguez): prefer conservative default thresholds (7d warning, 3d critical) and allow team overrides per initiative
PM review (Priya Nair): link initiative tranches to OKR subtargets so feature teams can see reliability credit for partial improvements

rollforward_plan: If initial nearline aggregation shows higher-than-expected latency or cost, fallback to daily rollups for low-cardinality cohorts and prioritize optimization for cohorts with highest customer impact. Schedule a retro after the first month of production to capture tuning parameters and update default thresholds. If the gating recommendations reduce release velocity unexpectedly, add opt-out at the team level and surface rationale in the release notes.
